name: The penitent thief
summary: Two malefactors were crucified with Christ. One railed on him; the other rebuked his fellow: we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward of our deeds, but this man hath done nothing amiss. Then: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
offense: Matthew calls them thieves, Luke malefactors; the man's own confession is that the sentence was just. He owned the law's verdict on himself in the hour of its execution.
judgment: The sentence of the state was carried out; he died on the cross that day. The sentence of heaven was reversed in the same hour: verily I say unto thee, to day shalt thou be with me in paradise. Isaiah had said the servant would be numbered with the transgressors.

entries.commentary: They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

Who has believed the report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed. He grows up before him as a tender plant and a root out of dry ground, with no form nor comeliness and no beauty that we should desire him. He is despised and rejected of men, a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief; we hid our faces from him and esteemed him not, though he bore our griefs and carried our sorrows. He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our iniquities; the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, turned everyone to his own way, and the Lord laid on him the iniquity of us all.

He was oppressed and afflicted, yet opened not his mouth; he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter and as a sheep dumb before her shearers. He was taken from prison and from judgment and cut off from the land of the living for the transgression of the people. He made his grave with the wicked and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence and no deceit was in his mouth. It pleased the Lord to bruise him and make his soul an offering for sin, and by his knowledge shall his righteous servant justify many, for he shall bear their iniquities. This whole chapter is the sacrifice that Christ made, why he made it, what he went through, and the fact that he bore our sins. He poured out his soul unto death, was numbered with the transgressors, bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors. -

verses.text: And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.
And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?
And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left.
The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth.

Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.
